beats.subline: Friday, November 20, 2026 close — a brutal AI-driven selloff left stocks with their worst week since the pandemic, pushing the S&P 500 and Dow into correction territory.
beats.body: Chip and AI stocks led the rout: the Nasdaq Composite erased all its 2026 gains and the semiconductor index posted its worst week since 2001, Nvidia fell roughly 23% for the week amid a reported SEC accounting inquiry and congressional scrutiny of its chip-export practices, and Anthropic's newly listed shares slid further in just their second day of trading.

beats.headline: NATO's governing council meets in Brussels after confirming Russian missiles hit Polish soil
beats.body: Polish prosecutors determined that all three objects that crossed into Polish airspace on Friday were Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles manufactured late this year near Moscow; NATO's North Atlantic Council convened Monday to weigh a response after Secretary-General Mark Rutte pledged the alliance would defend 'every inch' of Polish territory, and Warsaw has asked for additional AWACS and fighter coverage along its eastern flank.

beats.headline: Beijing claims Trump told Xi the US 'does not support' Taiwan independence; Taipei disputes the account
beats.body: Xinhua reported that during their November 19 meeting in Shenzhen, Trump told Xi the United States 'does not support' Taiwan independence, but Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council called the account 'not factual' and the White House has neither confirmed nor denied it; Taiwanese scholars noted the phrasing matches Washington's decades-old formulation and said it doesn't signal any shift in US policy toward the island.

beats.headline: Attacks on tankers near the Strait of Hormuz hit their highest pace since the US-Iran war began
beats.body: At least 25 tankers have been struck by projectiles in and around the Strait of Hormuz in the past week, Al Jazeera reports, as Iran and Iran-aligned forces continue trading fire with US assets in the Gulf; Iran says it's retaliating for US strikes on its Hengam and Qeshm Island sites and for drone overflights, while US Central Command maintains a naval blockade and has denied an Iranian claim of hitting an American F-16.

beats.body: The Golden Dome budget fight and the Trump-class battleship/DDG(X) replacement plan were reported earlier last week and fall outside the 72-hour window; no new, dated military-technology development from a reputable outlet surfaced within that window.

beats.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, an agent that reviews, fixes and approves pull requests
beats.body: Available today in beta to Claude Team and Enterprise customers, Claude Ship bundles Anthropic's existing Code Review tool with two new agents, PR Steward and Claude Approvals, which can fix failing checks and decide what's ready to merge under team-set rules; Anthropic says pull requests merged by its own Claude Code team more than doubled between June and September while reverted changes fell by over 40%.

beats.headline: Bears running back Roschon Johnson carted off with an ankle injury against the Saints
beats.body: Johnson left Sunday's Week 11 game against New Orleans in the first quarter and did not return; head coach Ben Johnson said the ankle will be evaluated this week, and backup Salvon Ahmed saw extended work in relief with starter Kyle Monangai also still managing a turf-toe issue.

beats.body: Byron's season ended at the Phoenix finale, and the Rudy Fugle-to-Adam Wall crew-chief move for 2027 was already reported earlier this month; no new, non-spoiler Byron news from a reputable outlet surfaced within the 72-hour window.
